I read the complete held EO 12163 (44 FR 56673, Sept. 29, 1979): sec. 1-903(a)(1) provides 'The following are revoked: (1) Executive Order No. 10973 of November 3, 1961, as amended', with no exception; sec. 1-905 makes it effective Oct. 1, 1979; sec. 1-504 re-establishes the public-information function in the International Communication Agency (USIA's successor name), which is the counterpart of new sec. 304(a). That names EO 11796 by number and date and revokes the whole order. The savings exception preserves only liability for past violations, not the order's operation. Sec. 2 continues EO 11533 and the actions under it pursuant to Public Law 93-372, effective as of the close of July 30, 1974; that continuance rests on EO 11533 and the statute, not on EO 11796. status_research.rationale: I read the complete held EO 13572 (76 FR 24787, May 3, 2011): blocks property of persons responsible for human-rights abuses in Syria, expands the scope of the emergency declared in EO 13338, with Treasury/State implementing authority; no own term. I read the held EO 14312 (90 FR 29395, July 3, 2025, 'Providing for the Revocation of Syria Sanctions'): sec. 3(a) 'Effective July 1, 2025, I hereby terminate the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13338 ... and revoke that order, as well as Executive Order 13399, Executive Order 13460, Executive Order 13572 of April 29, 2011 (Blocking Property of Certain Persons with Respect to Human Rights Abuses in Syria), Executive Order 13573, and Executive Order 13582.' Sec. 3(b) (NEA sec. 202(a)) preserves only actions taken or pending proceedings, acts before July 1, 2025 and matured rights or penalties, not any continuing prohibition. status_research.rationale: I read the complete held EO 9380 (8 FR 13081, Sept. 25, 1943; the held extract also carries neighbouring orders and a contents page): para. 1 establishes the Foreign Economic Administration (FEA) in the Office for Emergency Management; para. 2 consolidates four offices and the functions transferred by EO 9361 into it; para. 3 lets the Administrator create units; para. 4 makes its functions run in conformity with State Department foreign policy and, as military operations permit, gives it control of liberated-area supply and procurement; para. 5 transfers personnel, property and funds; para. 6 bars use of Public Law 139 funds abroad by the Administrator except as approved by the War Mobilization Committee; para. 7 amends conflicting prior orders and makes the order effective on the Administrator taking office. No own term. I read the held text of EO 9630 (10 FR 12245, Sept. 27, 1945), Part I para. 1: 'The Foreign Economic Administration established by Executive Order No. 9380 of September 25, 1943 ... and its agencies except as otherwise provided in this order, and the office of the Administrator of the Foreign Economic Administration, are terminated and disposition shall be made of the affairs thereof according to the provisions of this Part.' Paras. 2-6 then transfer its functions to State (incl. the liberated-areas function of EO 9380 para. 4, para. 2(c)), RFC, Commerce and Agriculture; para. 13 sets transfer dates no later than Dec. 31, 1945; para. 12 keeps prior regulations and directives relating to transferred functions in effect, which preserves administrative actions but not EO 9380 as an operating order. Every operative paragraph of EO 9380 (1-6) runs through the FEA or the Administrator, so termination of the FEA ends the whole order, as with Bowditch's EO 9204. EO 9380 is not named as revoked; the ending is the termination of the entity it created. D6 self-check: later events in the history are EO 9385 (Oct. 6, 1943, adds food functions; I read it, an amendment before the ending), EO 9630 (the ending), and the catalog 'See' to EO 9361 (an earlier order). EO 9630 was itself amended by EO 9730/9731 (para. 8 of Part II, State Department personnel sentence) and EO 9919 (export-control delegation to Commerce), and EO 10945 (May 24, 1961) sec. 5(a)(5)-(6) supersedes export-control provisions of EO 9380 and EO 9630; none of these restores the FEA or mentions reviving EO 9380 (I grepped FEA/9380 in all of them). No own term ran out earlier. Residual: para. 7's amendments of conflicting prior orders are executed text changes in other orders, not a continuing norm of EO 9380. Provisional NO hypothesis.

I read the held text of EO 9603 (Aug. 25, 1945, 'Termination of Possession of Certain Property Taken by the Government'): all plants, mines, facilities and other property seized or taken 'under and pursuant to the following-described Executive orders, or amendments thereof, shall be returned to the owners thereof as soon as practicable', and the list includes 'No. 9593 of July 25, 1945'; any listed order in conflict is amended to the extent of conflict. The order does not use the word revoked, and 'as soon as practicable' fixes no first-end date, so this is a functional end by a later instrument that names the order, which I record as a hypothesis, not an adjudicated first end.
